doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing opposite Basie, Ray Charles and Dinah Washington; booking agency
summary: His septet toured widely, shared bills with famous names, and earned $400 a night through a booking agent.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So you were traveling a lot across the years after you came back?
Oh, yeah, and listen, I mean, all the time.
With the same group? For a while?
Oh, yeah, septet. Yeah, man, that's changed because I.
They had a name, too, didn't it?
Huh?
Didn't it have a name, too? James Moody and his -- ?
Septet.
Okay.
Know, James Moody and His Orchestra.
[laughs]
Orchestra, boy, there was 9 pieces! But it sounded good, man. It was a good little band, man, we would play, we'd play opposite a lot of different people.
Like?
Do you remember Count Basie?
Uh-huh. [affirmative]
Ray Charles used to open for us.
Really?

Oh, yeah, like when he Flat Head [phonetic sp.] and Hank Crawford [phonetic sp.]. They all would open up. [indiscernible]. Dinah Washington, when she wasn't doing too well, like, with her records, they'd put her with us because, man, I was hot! And man, and we'd split the -- the percentage. And then when I cooled down and she got hot, there wasn't any percentage splitting. [laughs]
Were you with the same record label? Is that why they did that?
No, it was -- it was the same booking agent.
Booking agent.
Ben Barr. [phonetic sp.] The Raven bought his place. The name of his place, his home, was The Raven. 'Cause he had the raven, you know.
Oh, yeah, that's right. That group. Uh-huh. [affirmative]
And they -- he called it The Raven. Booked The Raven.
I'm sure they made some money for him.
I'm telling you about it.
Yeah. [laughs]
They used to do it! Listen, man, I used to -- 7 pieces, $400 a night. And I know now when I look back, there was money on this table. I know that. But that's okay because, Lord, everybody's dead.
[laughs]
I'm still here. See what I mean? [laughs] Yep! The Lord looks after those, you know. Who know who that they made love to. [laughter]
